clue.text: Guitarist, singer, and actor

blocks.note: a bass is a singer with the lowest male voice
a player is an actor on the stage

explanation.surface: A list of a band's line-up: someone who plays guitar, sings and acts.
explanation.walkthrough: The commas suggest three separate people, but the first word is the definition and the other two join to make it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bass player plays the bass guitar, so is one kind of guitarist.

clue.text: Offshoot of British cattle farm

blocks.note: B is the standard abbreviation for British
a ranch is a large cattle farm

explanation.surface: A spin-off business started by a British cattle farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A branch is a limb growing out of a tree, or by extension any offshoot of a larger body.

clue.text: Son's become confused by talk over bike accessory

indicators.note: in a down clue, over suggests turning the word upside down so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
to addle is to become muddled
gab is idle chatter

explanation.surface: A boy gets muddled by a sales pitch about a cycling accessory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'talk over' reads as discuss, but 'over' is the signal to turn the word upside down in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddlebag is a pouch strapped behind a bicycle seat, a common cycling accessory.

clue.text: State of alarm, frightful in satanic spot

indicators.note: frightful suggests something dreadfully disordered, so the letters that follow are thrown about

blocks.note: the three words supply every letter

explanation.surface: Someone is terrified, trapped in a devilish place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word placing the alarm somewhere, but its letters are part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic stations is an idiom for a state of emergency and frantic alarm, from the naval call to battle positions.

clue.text: Turn up a hill

blocks.note: taken as written
a rise is a slope or small hill

explanation.surface: Walking up a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn up' reads as a direction to climb, but it means to appear.
explanation.definitionFit: To arise is to come into being or crop up, as a problem may turn up unexpectedly.

clue.text: Drop of lager during fine meal cooked at home

indicators.note: a drop is a tiny amount, so only the opening letter of the word is taken
during places one thing in the middle of another, as an event happens within a period
cooked food is transformed, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of lager
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sipping a little beer during a good dinner made at home.
explanation.walkthrough: EN FAMILLE is French for 'with the family', used in English to mean at home or informally.
explanation.definitionFit: The borrowed French phrase describes doing something among one's family, that is, at home.

clue.text: Miss with something to keep her hands warm

definitions.text: something to keep her hands warm

blocks.note: first meaning: to fumble or bungle a catch or shot

blocks.clueFragment: something to keep her hands warm
blocks.note: second meaning: a fur tube into which both hands are slipped

explanation.surface: A young lady with a winter accessory for her hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a young woman, matching 'her', but it is the verb to fail to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: To muff a chance is to bungle it, and a muff is a fur hand-warmer once carried by women.

clue.text: Article taken from grubby relative

indicators.note: taken from says one item is removed out of the word that follows

blocks.note: an is the indefinite article
grubby means dirty

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece lifted from a dirty tabloid about a family member.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing AN from UNCLEAN leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncle is a parent's brother, a family relative.

clue.text: Being smart, I take off to test opinion

blocks.note: fly is British slang for sharp or knowing
I is the Roman numeral one, and one can be A
to kite is to soar or fly up, as a kite does

explanation.surface: A smart person decides to leave in order to sound out views.
explanation.walkthrough: The parse is loose: smart gives FLY, I as one gives A, and take off is read as soar, which a kite does.
explanation.definitionFit: To fly a kite is an idiom for floating an idea to see how people react before committing to it.

clue.text: Extra charge made by a key teacher at university

blocks.note: taken as written
D is one of the musical keys
a don is a university lecturer, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A university lecturer runs up a fee for something.
explanation.definitionFit: An add-on is an additional item or cost tacked onto a basic price.

clue.text: Hotly pursuing filly, run unwisely round foremost of courses

indicators.note: acting unwisely suggests a disorderly course, so these letters are scrambled
foremost means the very front, so only the leading letter is kept
round tells us the scrambled letters wrap around another piece

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the first letter of courses

explanation.surface: A young mare rashly bolts around the racecourse in hot pursuit.
explanation.walkthrough: The racing scene makes 'run' and 'courses' look literal; both are just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In full cry describes hounds baying in eager chase, hence anyone hotly pursuing something.

clue.text: See tree ahead of group of trees in picture

blocks.note: the laburnum is a tree with hanging yellow flowers
a grove is a small group of trees

explanation.surface: An instruction to look at a tree standing before a copse in a painting.
explanation.walkthrough: Picture means a film here: Laburnum Grove is J. B. Priestley's 1933 comedy, filmed in 1936.
explanation.definitionFit: The title names a 1936 British film, and a film is called a picture.

clue.text: Without preparation? Pick a cosmetic

blocks.note: to do something cold is to do it unprepared, as in a cold call
the pick of a group is its best, its cream

explanation.surface: Someone choosing a beauty product on the spur of the moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Cold cream is an emollient cream used to cleanse and soften the skin, a classic cosmetic.

clue.text: Pound included in bill, for fish

indicators.note: included in means placed inside the word that follows

blocks.note: a bird's bill is its beak
L is the symbol for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A pound added to the bill to pay for fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bill' looks like an invoice; it is a bird's beak.
explanation.definitionFit: The bleak is a small silvery European freshwater fish.

clue.text: One to decline being cuddled by a vivacious, sexy-looking girl?

indicators.note: being cuddled by means held inside the arms of what follows

blocks.note: taken as written
bright means lively and cheerful
I is the Roman numeral for one
to fall is to go down or decline

explanation.surface: A man refuses to be embraced by a lively, attractive woman.
explanation.walkthrough: I TO FALL sits inside A BRIGHT. A bit of all right is British slang for an attractive person.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal British speech, a bit of all right means a sexually attractive person, typically a woman.

clue.text: I've to appear in FA team in this form of football

indicators.note: to appear in means to show up inside the letters that follow

blocks.note: taken as written: the Football Association
taken as written, without the apostrophe
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A player says they must turn out for a Football Association team.
explanation.definitionFit: Five-a-side is a form of football played by small teams of five on a reduced pitch.

clue.text: Crowd, carefree mostly, by the arena

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: gay in its older sense means light-hearted
taken as written
a ring is an arena, as for boxing or a circus

explanation.surface: A happy-go-lucky crowd hangs about outside the stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering is an assembly of people, as a crowd is.

clue.text: One cadet spinning a yarn

indicators.note: spinning turns things round and round, so these letters are mixed up

blocks.note: the two words supply every letter

explanation.surface: A trainee officer tells a tall story.
explanation.walkthrough: Spinning a yarn is the idiom for telling a story, so 'spinning' does double duty in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A yarn is an informal word for a story, and an anecdote is a short personal story.

clue.text: Opposing union may cause a financial problem

blocks.note: a negative answer is one opposing a proposal
Equity is the British actors' trade union

explanation.surface: A union that opposes management can cause money trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Negative equity is the situation when a property is worth less than the mortgage secured on it.

clue.text: Sound of seal in a small pen? Possibly

indicators.note: sound of tells us the word is to be heard rather than read

blocks.note: a signet is a small seal, as on a ring

explanation.surface: The noise of a seal heard inside a small enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: A pen is a female swan, so a young swan could be a small pen; the question mark and 'Possibly' admit it might be a young male.
explanation.definitionFit: A cygnet is a young swan, and a female swan is called a pen, so a cygnet may be a little one.

clue.text: Commanding Officer taken round state capital

indicators.note: taken round means wrapped around the word that follows

blocks.note: CO is the abbreviation for Commanding Officer
to air a view is to state it

explanation.surface: A senior officer is given a tour of a state capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state capital' looks like one phrase, but 'state' is a verb and 'capital' stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Cairo is the capital city of Egypt.

clue.text: Children - an important subject

blocks.note: first meaning: offspring, as in to die without heirs
second meaning: a matter under debate

explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes it read as a statement that children matter; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is a legal word for a person's offspring and also means a key topic for discussion.

clue.text: Henley gal adrift in river

indicators.note: something adrift floats out of place, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the two words supply every letter

explanation.surface: A girl from Henley, the Thames rowing town, floats loose on the river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Allegheny is a river in Pennsylvania and New York that joins the Monongahela at Pittsburgh.

clue.text: Ruled in Dublin? Edward?

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

blocks.note: spans the end of the city and the start of the name

explanation.surface: Asking whether King Edward reigned in Dublin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruled' suggests governing; it means marked with straight lines, as ruled paper is.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruled paper has printed lines across it, so it is lined.

clue.text: Old boy at meeting with a fixed idea

blocks.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a session is a meeting of a body

explanation.surface: A former pupil turns up at a meeting with one idea on his mind.
explanation.definitionFit: An obsession is an idea that persistently fills the mind, an idée fixe.

clue.text: Hunter - gold one - working

blocks.note: or is gold in heraldry
I is the Roman numeral one
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A hunter strikes gold with a working claim.
explanation.definitionFit: Orion is the giant hunter of Greek myth, also a constellation.

clue.text: Iron uniform

blocks.note: first meaning: to smooth out or level
second meaning: regular and consistent

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests pressing a uniform; 'Iron' is a verb meaning to make flat.
explanation.definitionFit: To even something out is to level it, and an even surface or rate is uniform.

clue.text: An encumbrance? No more with crew

blocks.note: something that is no more is dead
W is an abbreviation for with
an eight is a rowing crew

explanation.surface: A rowing crew no longer wants a passenger slowing it down.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadweight is a heavy inert load, so figuratively anything that burdens or encumbers.
